key_insight: K/Rb-based lead-free double perovskites β2SnGeX6 (X = Cl, Br, I) are predicted by DFT to be stable, ductile, and highly tunable from wide-gap photovoltaic absorbers to low-gap optoelectronic and thermoelectric materials.
engineering_relevance: The series offers a non-toxic, compositionally adjustable platform for designing solar absorbers, tandem-photoactive layers, and high-ZT waste-heat recovery materials.
method: DFT study of structural, mechanical, electronic, optical, and thermoelectric properties
Stability screening via formation energy, tolerance factor, and octahedral factor
Transport analysis using band structure, effective masses, lattice thermal conductivity, and ZT
evidence_signal: The abstract reports cubic stability across all six compounds, direct bandgaps tunable from 1.44 to 0.64 eV, and a peak thermoelectric figure of merit of ZT = 2.4 for K2SnGeI6 at 1000 K.
watch_item: These are theoretical predictions from DFT, so experimental synthesis, phase stability under real processing conditions, and defect/temperature effects still need validation.
paper_title: First-Principles Study of Novel Lead-Free Double Perovskite \b{eta}2SnGeX6 (\b{eta} = K, Rb; X = Cl, Br, I) for thermomechanical, optoelectronic and outstanding thermoelectric applications
